summary: The successor receipt a9f71d7a07454d058d818148f7479e8f (completed, exit 0) reproduced the witness in a clean copy with all seven comparisons complete and evaluated as holds: the re-added voter (node 3, voter true, leader 1 unchanged) had not returned after 1200 ms (index 7), released only with 'context deadline exceeded' at its own 2500 ms deadline (index 8), and its payload never reached any node's committed entries (index 9), while the never-removed member returned in 0 ms and committed (indices 11, 12) and the same node 3 call returned in 0 ms and committed after the forced leader change to node 2 at term 2 (indices 13, 15, 16). The interpretation for this experiment is attributed with both receipts (joint history: same fixed scenario lineage, only event naming changed), and the snapshot's own node-level test (node_test.go:352-385) is added as a normative anchor: intended blocking is scoped to 'does not know who the current leader is' and acceptance is expected once a leader is known, which is exactly the condition the blocked re-added voter satisfies, while re-addition is untested. No new experiment was submitted; the open discriminator is answered and no repeat would add evidence.
